name: Local and Air-Gapped Model Deployment
title: Local and Air-Gapped Model Deployment
answer: Local and air-gapped model deployment covers running a language model on hardware a legal team controls, either on a private network or on a machine with no outside connection at all. It sits at the meeting point of legal operations, IT infrastructure and information security, and it exists because privileged material, client confidences and matter files often cannot leave the firm's boundary. The scope runs from a single workstation running a small open-weight model to a rack of accelerators inside a data centre, and it includes the surrounding stack of storage, access control and logging. It is not the same as using a hosted assistant under a contract, because the model weights and the data both stay inside the perimeter.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Local and air-gapped model deployment covers running a language model on hardware a legal team controls, either on a private network or on a machine with no outside connection at all. It sits at the meeting point of legal operations, IT infrastructure and information security, and it exists because privileged material, client confidences and matter files often cannot leave the firm's boundary. The scope runs from a single workstation running a small open-weight model to a rack of accelerators inside a data centre, and it includes the surrounding stack of storage, access control and logging. It is not the same as using a hosted assistant under a contract, because the model weights and the data both stay inside the perimeter.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: What it runs on is a machine the firm owns or leases: a workstation with one or more graphics cards, a server with larger accelerators, or a private cluster behind a firewall. Air-gapped setups add a physical or logical break from the public internet, so updates, model downloads and licence checks have to be moved across by hand or through a controlled transfer process. Storage has to hold model weights, which are large files, plus the vector index or document store that retrieval depends on. Power, cooling, rack space and the people who maintain them are part of the picture, and so is the question of who holds the keys to the hardware.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work is done by choosing an open-weight model that fits the available memory, then serving it with a runtime such as llama.cpp, vLLM or Ollama, and pointing a chat interface or an API at that server. For document work, a retrieval layer indexes the firm's own files and passes relevant passages to the model at query time, which keeps answers grounded in material the team already holds. Evaluation is done on the firm's own tasks rather than on public benchmarks alone, because a model that scores well in general may still mishandle a clause or a citation. Prompts, system instructions and retrieval settings are versioned like any other internal tool, and a small pilot on non-sensitive matters usually comes before wider use.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk turn on where the model weights came from, what licence they carry and whether that licence permits the intended commercial use. Provenance matters for the training data behind a model, and for any documents fed into a retrieval index, since those may carry their own confidentiality or contractual limits. Air gaps reduce exposure to outside networks but do not remove the need for access control, audit logging, retention rules and a record of which model version produced which output. Privilege and client confidentiality obligations still apply, and a local deployment does not by itself satisfy them. Firms also weigh vendor support, patching and the risk of running an unmaintained model, and they keep a human review step for anything that leaves the team.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel is toward smaller, more capable open-weight models that run on modest hardware, and toward better tooling for serving, retrieval and evaluation inside a private network. Hardware accelerators with more memory per card make larger models practical on a single machine, which changes what a small team can host. At the same time, the gap between local and hosted systems narrows on capability but not on convenience, so the choice stays a trade between control and effort. Expect more attention to model provenance, licence clarity and audit trails as local deployment moves from experiment to routine infrastructure in legal work.
